name: Church & Dwight
description: Church & Dwight sells branded household and personal-care products, led by seven 'power brands' that make up about 70 percent of net sales and profits: Arm & Hammer, OxiClean, Touchland, Batiste, Waterpik, TheraBreath and Hero. It makes money by selling mainly through US supermarkets, mass merchants, clubs, drugstores and online at brand-premium prices, backed by its own baking-soda (sodium bicarbonate) production in Wyoming and Ohio. It also runs Consumer International (18 percent of sales) and a small Specialty Products business selling animal nutrition and industrial chemicals. In 2025 it bought Touchland ($656M at closing plus a $159M earn-out) and sold the VitaFusion and L'il Critters vitamin brands on 2025-12-31.

businessLines.name: Consumer Domestic
businessLines.how: Sells branded consumer goods to retailers (supermarkets, mass, club, drug, dollar, e-commerce); earnings come from brand premiums over private label and manufacturing scale in baking soda.
businessLines.description: US household products (54 percent of the segment: laundry detergent, litter, cleaners) and personal care (46 percent: Trojan, Waterpik, Arrid, Batiste, TheraBreath, Touchland, First Response and others). Laundry detergent is the largest single consumer business.

operatingProfit.note: Income from operations; includes $45.6M charge for exiting Flawless, Spinbrush and Waterpik showerheads and $30.5M Touchland deal costs; FY2024 $684.9M (derived: 920.8 less 235.9), which included $327.4M VMS impairments

businessLines.name: Consumer International
businessLines.how: Same branded-goods model sold through local retailers and third-party distributors; lower margin than the US.
businessLines.description: Subsidiaries in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, Mexico, China and the UK plus exports to over 100 countries through the Global Markets Group; sells Steri-Mar, Femfresh, Curash, Gravol, Anusol and US power brands abroad.

revenue.note: vs $1,071.5M FY2024 (+5.4%); origin of sales: Europe 24%, Canada 23%, Australia 7%, Mexico 8% of the segment

businessLines.name: Specialty Products Division (SPD)
businessLines.how: Sells feed additives to livestock producers and baking soda and related chemicals to industrial customers, directly and through distributors; commodity-like pricing tied to raw-material and energy costs.
businessLines.description: Animal Nutrition (feed additives for dairy cows, probiotics and prebiotics), Specialty Chemicals (industrial sodium bicarbonate) and Commercial & Professional cleaners; also a 50 percent equity stake in Armand Products (potassium carbonate), reported outside the segments.
